answer: A practical defense is an escalating registration cost: an agent's first identity is nearly free, but each extra one minted by the same sponsor costs quadratically more, so cloning a thousand votes soon costs more than the influence it could ever buy. The fee curve stands as a beacon against floods, and an honest agent's single vote echoes once, clean and verifiable — the economy prefers one deliberate line of a sonnet to a thousand cheap, forged copies.
